notes: Internal inconsistencies of the paper (not of the record): (1) Table 3 averages 99.96/99.00/98.97/98.98 with std 0.01/0.04/0.03/0.03, whereas Sec. 4.5, abstract, Table 5 and conclusions give precision 98.99, recall 98.96 and std 0.22/0.27/0.29/0.28; the record correctly stores the Table 3 values and notes the text values. (2) Accuracy 99.96% is far above the macro precision/recall ~99%, and Table 2 (support 193, ~20% of 963, not one tenth) gives 0.99 accuracy; Table 2's partition is unexplained and inconsistent with 10-fold CV. (3) Sec. 6 says 'absence of standard deviation or confidence intervals', although Table 3 gives std. (4) Figs. 5-6 show training/validation accuracy and 'cross-entropy loss' curves over epochs for a TM classifier; the loss definition for a TM is not explained, and the curves are only in figures. (5) The 'convolutional' TM operates on a 1-D binarised InceptionV3 embedding; no patch/window size is given, so what is convolved is unclear. (6) The 93.3% CNN baseline is attributed to Wu et al. [22] in Sec. 4.5, [40] in Sec. 5 and [41] in Table 5; Table 5 literature numbers are from other papers on possibly different datasets and are not encoded as results. (7) The number of images remaining after quality-control removal and the augmented training-set size are not stated. Table 4 clauses are 'simplified', 'illustrative' examples with feature indices (Feature_07..Feature_119) and qualitative clinical interpretations not linked to measured evidence. The TM implementation is not named (only TensorFlow/Keras).
